chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man inherited a slave, and he has partners in him, so he freed his share for the sake of Allah.

He عليه السلام said: If he frees his share to cause harm, while he is financially capable, he is liable to compensate the heirs. But if he frees his share for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then the portion of the one who freed is emancipated from the slave, and they use him in proportion to what they own in him. So if half of him remains, he works for them one day and has one day for himself. And if the partner frees his share harmfully, then there is no emancipation for him, because he intended to corrupt matters against the people, and the people revert to their shares.

key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: purely for the sake of Allah
key_terms.مُضَارَّةً: with the intent of causing harm to others

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one partner frees his share of a jointly owned slave?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling of partial emancipation of a jointly owned slave, distinguishing between sincere manumission and an act done to harm co-owners. It establishes that intention affects the legal effect: sincere emancipation applies to one's own share, while harmful action incurs liability or is not recognized.
